fieldDescription: When does a faction consider your polity a threat to its export business? All share values are sector export market shares as shown in the commodity info screens.
Master switch. Turning this off freezes all grievances (existing intel entries remain but stop accruing).
How often market shares are re-checked and grievances updated.
Your export share of a commodity must be at least this to draw any attention.
A faction only cares about commodities where it holds at least this share - a marginal producer is not a real competitor.
The faction must be among this many top producers of the commodity (not counting you) to hold a grievance over it.
Your share must be at least this fraction of the reference faction share before they notice you. Also the compliance target.
The grievance bar runs 0-600: diplomatic warning at 200, formal ultimatum at 400, enforcement at 600. Monthly progress per contested commodity is weightMult x (your share / their share), capped.
Scales how fast resentment accrues from each contested commodity.
Cap on monthly resentment from any single commodity.
A grievance intel entry opens when a faction's total monthly resentment reaches this.
At most this many grievances are open sector-wide at once - the angriest factions win the slots.
Monthly drain on the bar while the faction has no active causes against you (you complied, or your dominance lapsed).
Days of total calm (no causes, bar at zero) before a grievance is dropped and the intel entry ends.

At the ultimatum stage the faction accepts one-off settlement payments that buy down accumulated resentment - partial installments or a full settlement that clears the bar. Money is taken up front. The dispute itself remains as long as your dominance does.
A full settlement from max resentment (600) costs this many months of your contested export income; partial payments price per point off the same rate.
Floor on the full-settlement cost in credits.
For military grievances, the full-settlement basis is your military-industrial score times this - reparations scale with the arsenal they fear.

Factions grow uneasy when your military-industrial score (market sizes + patrol/military/command structures + stations + war industry; see Debug Mode) rivals their own. Demands: downgrade, settle, or take a commission with them (suppresses their concern while you serve; resigning spikes resentment). Military-track strikes target your most militarized colony.
Your military score must reach this fraction of a faction's own before they grow uneasy.
Below this military score, nobody considers your arsenal worth an ultimatum.
Scales how fast military resentment accrues (mult x yourScore / theirScore).
Cap on monthly resentment from the military cause.
Resentment gained instantly when you resign or lose a commission that was holding a military grievance at bay.

When the bar hits 600 the faction launches an enforcement strike at your top producer of the contested commodities. Difficulty = base x (1 + escalation x mult). Each defeated strike raises escalation. At the escalation threshold, strikes switch from disruption raids to tactical bombardment. Successful strikes steal contested commodities from the target's storage and are followed by a truce.

Minimum statement-force budget of an enforcement strike (10 = roughly one full-size fleet). Actual budget aims to overmatch the target's defenses, escalates with defiance, and is capped by the faction's military-industrial capacity.
Strikes aim for this multiple of the target system's defense strength (patrols + battlestation) - enough to ensure victory, not a token gesture.
Conversion between measured fleet strength and strike difficulty points. Higher = smaller strikes for the same defenses. Tune with Debug Mode's strike math line.

Fraction of a faction's military-industrial score it will commit to one enforcement strike. Their infrastructure (bases, stations, war industry - disrupted structures do not count) is the hard ceiling: no magic fleets.
Difficulty multiplier gained per escalation level (defeated strike).
Hard cap on enforcement strike difficulty.
Bar value the grievance resets to when a strike launches.
Bar value the grievance falls to when you defeat an enforcement strike - the setback is real, and resentment must climb all the way back before they try again.
Minimum days after a strike resolves (win or lose) before the same faction can launch another, no matter how fast the bar refills.
Days of frozen accrual after a successful enforcement strike (they made their point).
Escalation level at which strikes switch from disruption raids to tactical bombardment.

Fraction of contested commodities in the target colony's resource stockpiles and storage carried off by a successful strike. The loot lands in the source market's open market - visible, and buyable back.
How long plundered commodities suffer an availability penalty on the raided market (a real econ effect on top of the raid's industry disruption).
Size of the availability penalty on plundered commodities (in supply units, like a shortage).

At high escalation, strikes go after installed items (nanoforge, synchrotron...) in grievance-relevant industries. A heist is a ground operation: it targets ground defenses and heavy batteries, and needs marines - defender strength x overmatch - constrained by the faction's actual marine production. Stolen items are re-installed on the faction's own markets and can be raided back.
Escalation level at which strikes attempt item heists (if a stealable item exists and they can muster the marines).
Marines required = target ground defender strength x this.
Converts a faction's marine production (in supply units) into marines it can muster for one operation.
How long the faction's marine availability is visibly depressed at its producing markets after mustering a heist.
Size of the marine availability penalty while mustered.

A faction only presses demands while its military-industrial score - pooled with coalition partners (mutually non-hostile aggrieved factions) - reaches gateRatio x yours. Too weak: resentment simmers below the ultimatum line ('Deterred by your strength'). Coalition strikes field mixed fleets; defeating one can demoralize partners out of the pool. Outgrow every plausible coalition and the demands stop: earned silence.
Master toggle for the strength gate. Off = factions press demands regardless of relative power (pre-Phase-5 behavior).

A faction with an actively-rolled vanilla colony crisis EVENT (an imminent attack) gets no Commerce Wars grievance on top - no simultaneous double coercion. Baseline background pressure (AI-core use, colony size, fuel) does NOT defer, since it never stops. Existing grievances freeze (and hide) only while a crisis event is rolled.

Strips story-critical protection from every market: any world can be saturation-bombed down (size -1 per bombardment) and destroyed at size 4 or below - factions can be entirely eliminated, with elimination announced. WARNING: questlines anchored on destroyed worlds will strand.

Saturation-bombing a faction converts its grievance into a permanent Blood Feud: no settlements, tribute, truces, or expiry - a fixed blood-debt drive cycles toward saturation-bombardment reprisals against your worlds, bounded only by their real military capacity and the strength gate. Ends when one side has no worlds left.
Sat-bombing a faction starts (or deepens) a blood feud instead of a mere resentment spike.
Bar value a blood feud starts at (or is raised to) when declared.
Base monthly drive toward reprisal in a blood feud.

Extra monthly drive per point of the faction's military-industrial score - great powers avenge relentlessly, broken rump states only sporadically. Cripple their military to slow (never stop) the feud.
Fraction of the player's military score a faction (plus partners) must muster to press demands.
Chance for each coalition partner to lose its stomach when a coalition strike is defeated.
How long a demoralized faction stays out of coalition pools.
A faction only lends its strength to coalition partners while its own grievance bar is at least this - settle a member below the line to buy them out of the pact.

Your own raids and bombardments against a faction with an active grievance spike its resentment instantly - and can trigger enforcement outright (still subject to the strength gate and strike cooldown). Saturation bombardment ripples: emboldened rivals grow hotter, weak ones are cowed out of coalition pools.
Resentment gained when you raid one of their markets.
Resentment gained when you tactically bombard one of their markets.
Resentment gained when you saturation-bombard one of their markets.
Resentment gained by OTHER emboldened aggrieved factions when you saturation-bombard anyone - if you did it to them, who is next?
Development tools. Debug Mode reveals every internal number on the grievance intel screen - shares, weights, thresholds, timers.
Reveal all internal stats on grievance intel screens (shares, raw weights, thresholds, timers).
Verbose [CommWars] lines in starsector.log.
Multiplies all resentment accrual by 10 for rapid testing.
If no grievance is active, opens one against the best candidate faction on the next tick, ignoring the start threshold. Great for seeing the intel screen without an export empire.
Every tick, jumps the angriest active grievance to the ultimatum stage. Toggle off after use.
Every tick, pushes the angriest active grievance to the enforcement stage, launching a strike if none is active. Toggle off after use.
